#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update/supersede policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; after `version` commits, HEAD intentionally changes.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs initial enriched number repository branch workflow_delta
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository)
  initial=$(jq -c '[.[] | {
    number,
    headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
    headBranch: .headRefName,
    workflowDeltaFromBase: false
  }]' <<< "$raw_prs")
  enriched='[]'

  # This is forge/Git observation, not policy: fetch every safe same-repository
  # PR branch and report whether its workflow files differ from the checked-out
  # base. Callisto decides whether that fact requires a replacement PR.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r number repository branch; do
    workflow_delta=false
    if [[ "$repository" == "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" ]] && git check-ref-format --branch "$branch" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      git fetch --no-tags origin "refs/heads/$branch:refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
      if ! git diff --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$branch...HEAD" -- .github/workflows; then
        workflow_delta=true
      fi
    fi
    enriched=$(jq -c \
      --argjson number "$number" \
      --arg repository "$repository" \
      --arg branch "$branch" \
      --argjson workflow_delta "$workflow_delta" \
      '. + [{number: $number, headRepository: $repository, headBranch: $branch, workflowDeltaFromBase: $workflow_delta}]' \
      <<< "$enriched")
  done < <(jq -r '.[] | [.number, .headRepository, .headBranch] | @tsv' <<< "$initial")

  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson open_pull_requests "$enriched" \
    '{schemaVersion: 1, repository: $repository, baseBranch: $base_branch, baseCommit: $base_commit, openPullRequests: $open_pull_requests}'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  supersede)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.replacementBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
"${command[@]}"
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }
if [[ "$INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER" == true ]]; then
  git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
  git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
fi
git switch -C "$release_branch"
git add -A
git commit -m "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"

# A local commit does not authorize a stale force-push. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
current_snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$current_snapshot" > /dev/null
git push --force-with-lease origin "$release_branch"

current_snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$current_snapshot" > /dev/null

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  supersede)
    new_pr_url=$(gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL")
    gh pr close "$existing_pr" --comment "Superseded by $new_pr_url because GitHub requires elevated workflow authority to update this generated branch. The replacement was recomputed from the current base branch and pending changesets."
    ;;
esac

content.text: That's normal serde_json serialization, so the enum's own `#[serde(...)]` attribute is the bug. Let me double check the actual derive attribute on the enum in the source (maybe rename_all doesn't apply to internally-tagged variant fields as I assumed — let's verify serde's actual behavior).

Root cause found. `ReleasePrActionV1` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs` has `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind", ...)]`, but serde's `rename_all` only camelCases the variant tag (`"kind": "supersede"`), not the fields *inside* each variant — those still serialize as snake_case (`pull_request_number`, not `pullRequestNumber`). The shell script does `jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber'`, which then reads `null`, and `gh pr view null` fails with "no pull requests found for branch \"null\"" — exactly the CI error.

Confirmed by reproducing locally: built `callisto` from the exact failing commit and ran `release-pr decide` against the real PR #28 snapshot — output shows `"pull_request_number"` and `"expected_branch"` in snake_case despite the `camelCase` directive.

The fix is `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` (needs serde ≥1.0.166) alongside `rename_all`. Let me check the serde version and same-named enum `ReleasePrNoopReasonV1`.

content.text:
Opened https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/47.

**Root cause:** `ReleasePrActionV1` (crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs) is an internally-tagged enum with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")]`. That attribute only camelCases the variant tag value — it doesn't rename fields *inside* variants, a known serde gotcha. So `pull_request_number`/`expected_branch`/`replacement_branch` serialized as snake_case even though `"kind"` correctly came out as `"supersede"`.

`create-or-update-release-pr.sh` does `jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber'`, got `null` back, and ran `gh pr view null` — `gh` treats a non-numeric arg as a branch name, producing exactly the observed error: `no pull requests found for branch "null"`.

Introduced in PR #46 ("make Callisto own release PR decisions", merged into main at bfc59f5e), which is the exact commit the failing run pinned to.

**Fix:** add `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` alongside `rename_all`, plus a regression test asserting the JSON shape. Verified by building the pre-fix binary against the repo's real open managed PR (#28) — reproduced the bug (`pull_request_number` in output) — then rebuilt with the fix and confirmed `pullRequestNumber` comes through correctly.

Cut PR #47 off `main` with the fix, a changeset, and a `cargo test -p callisto-model` regression test — all passing. Once merged, the release workflow should work again on the next push to main.
Are we sure this is the only issue?
Let me not assume — I'll trace the rest of the script and check for other jq/CLI-shape mismatches, plus what happens downstream (publish/tag steps) that haven't even been reached yet.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
  fi
done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

No — I found one more instance of the same bug pattern, plus a real gap in test coverage that's *why* this shipped. Here's what I checked:

**1. The fix is correct and sufficient for the failure that happened.** Confirmed by rebuilding the exact failing commit and replaying the real PR #28 snapshot through it before/after the patch.

**2. Why existing tests didn't catch it — a real gap:** `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh` is the dedicated contract test for this script, but it stubs `callisto` out entirely with hand-written, already-correct camelCase JSON fixtures (`$create`, `$update`, `$supersede`). It never invokes the real compiled binary, so it can't catch a mismatch between what serde actually emits and what the shell script's `jq` expects. That's a structural blind spot, not just bad luck — worth hardening (e.g., one case that shells out to the real `callisto` binary against a synthetic snapshot) so this class of bug can't recur silently.

**3. Same bug pattern exists elsewhere:** I grepped for every `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind", ...)]` enum in `callisto-model` and checked each variant's fields. Most are single-word field names (`sha`, `slot`, `reason`) where snake_case and camelCase are identical, so they're harmless. One real hit: `ReleaseInclusionReason` in `crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:257` has `LinkedGroup { group_id }`, `FixedGroup { group_id }`, `Cascade { from, edge_kind }`, `PreReleasePolicy { policy_id }` — same casing bug, `group_id`/`edge_kind`/`policy_id` come out snake_case despite the camelCase directive.

   Currently this one is **not causing a live failure** — I checked every shell script and found nothing that reads `groupId`/`edgeKind`/`policyId` via `jq`; it's only consumed internally by Rust (`compose-pr-body`, changelog rendering). But it's the same latent trap, and it'll bite the next time something external starts parsing that field.

I did not attempt to dry-run the rest of the durable pipeline (`plan` → `build` → `execute`, attestation, environment-approval gating) — those jobs never even ran in the failing workflow, so I can't empirically verify them, and I didn't want to poke at the release-execution path without your say-so.

It never once calls the real `callisto` binary, so it structurally cannot detect a shape mismatch between what serde actually emits and what `jq` expects — which is exactly the bug that took prod down. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_release_pr_contract.sh stubs `callisto` with hand-written camelCase
# JSON fixtures, so it only proves the script's control flow given already
# correctly-shaped input -- it structurally cannot catch a mismatch between
# what the real binary serializes and what this script's `jq` expects. That
# gap is exactly how a snake_case regression in ReleasePrActionV1 (fields
# inside a #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")] enum are NOT
# renamed by rename_all -- only the tag is) shipped to production and broke
# every release run past the first (`gh pr view null`, from `jq -r
# '.action.pullRequestNumber'` reading a field that didn't exist).
#
# This test compiles and calls the real `callisto` binary and asserts the
# exact `jq` expressions this action's script uses against its real output.
set -euo pipefail

action_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
workspace_root="$(cd "$action_dir/../../.." && pwd)"
script="$action_dir/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh"

cargo build -p callisto-cli --quiet --manifest-path "$workspace_root/Cargo.toml"
callisto_bin="$workspace_root/target/debug/callisto"

fail=0

assert_jq_matches_real_output() {
  local label="$1" workflow_delta="$2" expect_kind="$3"
  local snapshot decision decision_kind existing_pr

  snapshot=$(jq -cn \
    --arg repository 'orin-dx/callisto' \
    --arg base_branch main \
    --arg base_commit '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567' \
    --argjson workflow_delta "$workflow_delta" \
    '{schemaVersion: 1, repository: $repository, baseBranch: $base_branch, baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [{number: 42, headRepository: $repository, headBranch: "callisto/version-packages",
      workflowDeltaFromBase: $workflow_delta}]}')

  decision=$("$callisto_bin" --format json release-pr decide \
    --snapshot "$snapshot" --repository orin-dx/callisto --base-branch main \
    --release-branch callisto/version-packages --cwd "$workspace_root")

  # These are the exact expressions create-or-update-release-pr.sh evaluates.
  decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
  existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")

  if [[ "$decision_kind" != "$expect_kind" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL ($label): expected decision kind '$expect_kind', got '$decision_kind': $decision"
    fail=1
    return
  fi
  if [[ "$existing_pr" != "42" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL ($label): jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' resolved to '$existing_pr' instead of 42 -- this is exactly what made the script run \`gh pr view null\`: $decision"
    fail=1
    return
  fi
  echo "PASS ($label): real binary output round-trips through the script's jq expressions"
}

# has_pending_changesets must be true against this workspace for either case
# below to produce anything but a noop -- true as long as a changeset file
# is pending, which this repository's own release process requires anyway.
if [[ -z "$(find "$workspace_root/.changeset" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
  echo 'SKIP: no pending changesets in this checkout; cannot exercise update/supersede decisions'
  exit 0
fi

assert_jq_matches_real_output 'update (no workflow delta)' false update
assert_jq_matches_real_output 'supersede (workflow delta)' true supersede

if ! grep -q "$script" <(echo "$script"); then
  : # keep shellcheck quiet about an otherwise-unused variable in trivial runs
fi

exit "$fail"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_release_pr_contract.sh stubs `callisto` with hand-written camelCase
3	# JSON fixtures, so it only proves the script's control flow given already
4	# correctly-shaped input -- it structurally cannot catch a mismatch between
5	# what the real binary serializes and what this script's `jq` expects. That
6	# gap is exactly how a snake_case regression in ReleasePrActionV1 (fields
7	# inside a #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")] enum are NOT
8	# renamed by rename_all -- only the tag is) shipped to production and broke
9	# every release run past the first (`gh pr view null`, from `jq -r
10	# '.action.pullRequestNumber'` reading a field that didn't exist).
11	#
12	# This test compiles and calls the real `callisto` binary and asserts the
13	# exact `jq` expressions this action's script uses against its real output.
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	action_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
17	workspace_root="$(cd "$action_dir/../../.." && pwd)"
18	
19	cargo build -p callisto-cli --quiet --manifest-path "$workspace_root/Cargo.toml"
20	callisto_bin="$workspace_root/target/debug/callisto"
21	
22	fail=0
23	
24	assert_jq_matches_real_output() {
25	  local label="$1" workflow_delta="$2" expect_kind="$3"
26	  local snapshot decision decision_kind existing_pr
27	
28	  snapshot=$(jq -cn \
29	    --arg repository 'orin-dx/callisto' \
30	    --arg base_branch main \
31	    --arg base_commit '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567' \
32	    --argjson workflow_delta "$workflow_delta" \
33	    '{schemaVersion: 1, repository: $repository, baseBranch: $base_branch, baseCommit: $base_commit,
34	      openPullRequests: [{number: 42, headRepository: $repository, headBranch: "callisto/version-packages",
35	      workflowDeltaFromBase: $workflow_delta}]}')
36	
37	  decision=$("$callisto_bin" --format json release-pr decide \
38	    --snapshot "$snapshot" --repository orin-dx/callisto --base-branch main \
39	    --release-branch callisto/version-packages --cwd "$workspace_root")
40	
41	  # These are the exact expressions create-or-update-release-pr.sh evaluates.
42	  decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
43	  existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
44	
45	  if [[ "$decision_kind" != "$expect_kind" ]]; then
46	    echo "FAIL ($label): expected decision kind '$expect_kind', got '$decision_kind': $decision"
47	    fail=1
48	    return
49	  fi
50	  if [[ "$existing_pr" != "42" ]]; then
51	    echo "FAIL ($label): jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' resolved to '$existing_pr' instead of 42 -- this is exactly what made the script run \`gh pr view null\`: $decision"
52	    fail=1
53	    return
54	  fi
55	  echo "PASS ($label): real binary output round-trips through the script's jq expressions"
56	}

62	  echo 'SKIP: no pending changesets in this checkout; cannot exercise update/supersede decisions'

content.text:
Pushed to PR #47. Now, to your question directly:

**Yes — this is a systemic pattern, not a one-off.** Every "contract test" for the release action under `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/` and `.github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/` fakes `callisto`, `gh`, and `git` as bash functions. Most of them (`test_native_artifact_placement.sh`, `test_status_check_branching.sh`, `test_tag_push_force.sh`, `test_github_release_creation.sh`, etc.) use an `extract_snippet` helper that pulls the *actual* shell body out of `action.yml`, so the control-flow logic under test is real — only the external tool calls are faked, which is a reasonable boundary for testing shell logic in isolation.

The dangerous version of this is specifically: **wherever a faked `callisto` subcommand's JSON output is hand-typed instead of generated by the real binary**, because that fixture silently encodes an assumption about serde's output shape that can drift from reality with zero warning. That's exactly what happened with `release-pr decide` → `ReleasePrActionV1`.

I checked whether this is currently drifting anywhere else:
- `test_release_pr_contract.sh` — confirmed drifting (now fixed, PR #47).
- `test_publish_partial_failure_filters_plan.sh` fakes `callisto publish`/`filter-plan`/`plan-publish` output by hand too. I checked the real struct behind it (`PublishAttemptResult` in `report.rs`) — someone already got burned by this exact class of bug there and hard-coded `#[serde(rename = "errorKind")]` on that field instead of trusting `rename_all`. So that fixture currently matches reality, but by an explicit patch, not because the test would catch drift if it happened again.
- Same story for `test_native_matrix_dedup.sh` (fakes `callisto matrix` output) and `test_github_release_creation.sh` — I didn't find live drift, but none of them would notice if one appeared.

So: no other **currently-broken** instance found, but the test suite has no structural defense against this bug class recurring — it only doesn't happen to be wrong right now, in three or four other places, by luck plus one prior manual fix. If you want, I can add real-binary contract tests (like the one I just wrote) for `matrix`, `plan-publish`/`filter-plan`, and `compose-pr-body` too, so the whole action test suite stops trusting hand-typed JSON for anything that crosses the Rust→shell boundary. Want me to do that now in the same PR, or as a separate follow-up?

No, not confused — and the diff above proves the point rather than complicating it: PR #28 touched **zero** workflow files. Only changesets, CHANGELOGs, and Cargo.toml version bumps — exactly what a release PR should be. That rule held.

The `workflow_delta_from_base` check is about something else entirely, and I should've separated these two ideas more clearly last time:

- **What the release PR contains**: never workflow files. Confirmed above.
- **What triggered supersede**: #28's branch was cut from `main` on Aug 28. Since then, PRs #38–#46 rewrote `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` on `main` itself (1.8K → 9K, added the durable pipeline). So *`main`'s own workflow files moved forward* while #28 sat open with the old ones.

To "update" #28 in place, the script would force-push `main` + version-bump onto that same branch name — and since `main`'s workflows have since changed, that push would necessarily overwrite the branch's stale workflow files with the current ones. That's a real change to `.github/workflows/*` content on that ref, and GitHub's `GITHUB_TOKEN` categorically cannot push that, on any branch, regardless of why. So Callisto detects the situation ahead of time and cuts a brand-new branch off current `main` instead — which starts in sync with `main`'s workflows, so it never needs to touch them either.

So: release PRs still never contain workflow changes. What changed is that *upstream `main`* did, out from under a stale open PR, and that's specifically what forced the supersede instead of a plain update.
But those were merged in another PR so we should have been able to just rebase the release branch and it should not have included the workflow, right?

No — a rebase wouldn't have sidestepped this, and I want to be precise about why, since it's a fair thing to push back on.

The GitHub restriction isn't about *how* the branch gets updated (merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or fresh recreation) — it's purely about *whether the final pushed tree differs from what's currently on that ref at `.github/workflows/*`*. That check is content-based, not mechanism-based.

Walk through what a rebase would actually produce here: `git rebase main` on #28's branch replays its one version-bump commit on top of current `main`. The resulting tree is: current `main`'s tree + the version-bump diff. That's *exactly* the same final tree the "recreate from scratch" approach (`git switch -C` off current `main`, then commit) produces — there's no merge conflict to resolve differently, so rebase and recreate converge on the identical result.

And that resulting tree necessarily has `main`'s *current* `.github/workflows/*` content — which differs from what's sitting on the remote `callisto/version-packages` ref right now (the old, pre-#38–46 files). So pushing the rebased branch would need to overwrite `.github/workflows/*` on that ref, same as pushing the recreated one. Same wall either way: `GITHUB_TOKEN` has no `workflows` write scope — it's not something you can even grant via the workflow's `permissions:` block, unlike `contents` or `pull-requests`. It's hard-excluded from the token's permission set entirely. A PAT or GitHub App token with actual workflow-write permission could do it; the automatic token categorically can't, regardless of git plumbing.

So the fix isn't "rebase instead of recreate" — both hit the identical push rejection. The only way to update in place would be to hand the job a more privileged token, which is exactly the kind of privilege expansion the last few PRs (#39/#43/#46, "release trust"/"durable attested release") were deliberately trying to *avoid*. Superseding is the tradeoff of keeping the token minimally privileged.

I don't have a record of that. Scrolling back through this conversation, "rebase" first came up in your last message — I haven't agreed to it or discussed it before that. If this was covered in an earlier session or a conversation I don't have visibility into, I don't have that context here.

On the substance, my answer stands regardless of what was said before: a rebase and a from-scratch recreation of the branch produce the identical final tree in this situation (no conflicts to resolve differently), so they hit the identical GitHub restriction on `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushing to `.github/workflows/*`. That's a fact about git/GitHub mechanics, not a position I'm holding for its own sake — if you have a concrete counter-scenario where rebase produces a different resulting tree than recreation, I'd genuinely like to see it, since that would change the analysis. But I'm not going to say I agreed with something I have no record of agreeing to.

I found several relevant results about this GitHub issue. Here's what the web search revealed:

## Root Cause

GitHub blocks the automatically-issued GITHUB_TOKEN from creating or updating any file under .github/workflows/ so that a compromised action cannot rewrite the repository's automation to escalate its own privileges.

## Solutions

### For Personal Access Tokens (PAT)
To modify a workflow file from an actions workflow, you must use a personal access token. To make changes to a workflow file and commit it, these repo scopes are required: contents:write, workflows:write.

### Important: Token Configuration in Checkout
A critical detail many people miss: Setting the token on your git push step does nothing, because actions/checkout already configured the git credentials at the start of the job, and those are the credentials the push uses. Wire the PAT into checkout from the start rather than waiting for the first workflow-file diff to break the pipeline.

### When Using GitHub Apps
The GITHUB_TOKEN doesn't have access to the workflows permission. If you want to update a file in .github/workflows, you'd need a personal access token, or to use an app with the proper configuration.

### Workaround for Synced Workflows
The error happens because the branch contains changes in .github/workflows compared to the default branch. To solve this, you can checkout the default branches files into your new branch, commit those changes and you're synced and allowed to push.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Creates or refreshes the non-privileged Callisto release PR. This script is
+# intentionally the composite action's executable implementation so its tests
+# exercise the exact code a GitHub runner invokes.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+cd "$INPUT_CWD"
+
+set +e
+callisto status --check
+status=$?
+set -e
+case "$status" in
+  1) echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
+  2)
+    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
+    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
+    exit 0
+    ;;
+  *) echo "::error::callisto status --check exited $status"; exit 1 ;;
+esac
+
+# A managed branch must have at most one open PR to its configured base. The
+# SHA-suffixed form is an automatic GitHub-token fallback used only when
+# updating the long-lived branch would cross a workflow file change.
+prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,body,headRefName,headRepository \
+  --jq '[.[] | select(.headRepository.nameWithOwner == env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY and (.headRefName == env.INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH or ((.headRefName | startswith(env.INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH + "--")) and ((.headRefName | ltrimstr(env.INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH + "--")) | test("^[0-9a-f]{40}$")))))]')
+pr_count=$(jq 'length' <<< "$prs")
+case "$pr_count" in
+  0) existing='' ;;
+  1) existing=$(jq -r '.[0].body // empty' <<< "$prs") ;;
+  *) echo "::error::found $pr_count open release PRs for $INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH -> $INPUT_BRANCH"; exit 1 ;;
+esac
+
+if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
+  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
+else
+  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
+fi
+active_branch=$(jq -r '.[0].headRefName // empty' <<< "$prs")
+if [[ -z "$active_branch" ]]; then
+  active_branch="$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH"
+fi
+
+# Rebuild the generated release commit from the current base branch on every
+# run. A literal rebase would preserve stale generated version, changelog, and
+# changeset-deletion edits rather than recomputing them. GitHub's installation
+# token rejects force-updating an old managed ref when its replacement crosses
+# an already-reviewed workflow change on the base branch. In that narrow case
+# rotate to a deterministic SHA-suffixed managed branch.
+release_branch="$active_branch"
+if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "refs/heads/$active_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+  git fetch --no-tags origin "refs/heads/$active_branch:refs/remotes/origin/$active_branch"

Found the actual answer, and it's better sourced than either of us was working from. Here's the exact comment from the commit that introduced this (`94788abb`, "feat(action): preserve managed release PR continuity"):

> A literal rebase would preserve stale generated version, changelog, and changeset-deletion edits rather than recomputing them. GitHub's installation token rejects force-updating an old managed ref when its replacement crosses an already-reviewed workflow change on the base branch. In that narrow case rotate to a deterministic SHA-suffixed managed branch.

Two separate things going on, and I'd conflated them:

1. **Why it's never a literal `git rebase`, independent of GitHub's restriction:** the version bump, changelog entries, and changeset deletions are *generated* content — output of running `callisto version` fresh against whatever changesets are currently pending. A rebase would replay the *old* generated diff (computed against whatever changesets existed when it was last generated) onto a new base, not regenerate it. If changesets changed since, that replayed diff would be stale/wrong. So this system always reruns `callisto version` from scratch on every pass — mechanically that produces the same tree a clean rebase would in the case where nothing changed, but it's correct in the case where something did.

2. **The GitHub token restriction specifically, on force-updating an *existing* ref:** this comment states it as tested/observed fact by whoever built it — force-pushing new content to an existing branch is rejected when that update crosses a workflow-file change on the base, regardless of whether the pushed content matches current `main` exactly. I was reasoning about this from memory/analogy earlier and got pushed into uncertain territory when you pressed on it; this is first-party evidence from the actual builder of this exact system, on this exact scenario, so I trust it over my own recollection or the generic web results I pulled (which described a related but not identical scenario — syncing a *stale* branch, not force-updating a GitHub-tracked one after the fact).

**On your second question — no, and I should've said this more plainly the first time:** Callisto does not modify workflow files in repos that use it. PR #28's actual diff (confirmed earlier) touched zero workflow files — only changesets, changelogs, and `Cargo.toml` versions. The `workflow_delta_from_base` check exists specifically so Callisto's token *never* touches `.github/workflows/*` — when it detects that updating in place would require crossing that boundary, it refuses and opens a clean branch instead. That check is a safeguard against exactly the risk you're worried about, not evidence of it happening.
We should run that detection AFTER rebasing though. I suspect you're doing it before

Checked precisely — your instinct about ordering mattering is the right kind of thing to suspect, but it doesn't apply here, and I can show why rather than just assert it.

Look at the actual sequence in `create-or-update-release-pr.sh`:

```
1. workflow_delta = git diff refs/remotes/origin/$old_branch...HEAD -- .github/workflows   # computed here
2. decision = callisto release-pr decide --snapshot ...
3. callisto version                                                                         # the "rebase"-equivalent step
4. git switch -C $release_branch; git add -A; git commit; git push
```

The workflow-delta check (step 1) does run *before* the version-bump step (step 3) — so your suspicion about the order is literally correct as stated. But it doesn't matter in practice, because I checked what `callisto version` (step 3) actually touches: `plan_version`/`apply_version_plan` in `callisto-graph` only ever read/write `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` manifests, `CHANGELOG.md` files, and `.changeset/*.md`. I grepped the whole command path — zero references to `.github/workflows` anywhere.

So step 3 never changes `.github/workflows` content at all. That means computing the diff at step 1 (before step 3) versus computing it after step 3 gives the *identical* answer — `HEAD`'s `.github/workflows` tree is the same before and after the version bump, because nothing in that step touches that path. The check is really just "does the old PR's branch differ from current `main` at this path" — a fact fixed by history, not something the version-bump step could change either way.

Where your general concern *would* be valid: if the version-bump step (or anything else in the pipeline) ever wrote to `.github/workflows`, then yes, checking before vs. after would give different, and the "before" check would be wrong/stale. It doesn't here, but it's a fair thing to have flagged and worth a code comment noting the invariant, since right now that safety only holds because of what `callisto version` happens not to touch, not because the ordering was chosen deliberately to guarantee it. Want me to add an explicit assertion/comment (or move the check after step 3 defensively) so this doesn't silently break if `version` ever starts writing outside its current scope?
The workflow delta need to be computed accounting for the rebase then, no?

Structurally, no — it *can't* run strictly after the rebase, because the decision (create/update/supersede) determines what branch to commit onto, so it has to happen before `callisto version` runs. That's a real chicken-and-egg constraint, not an oversight.

But here's the thing that makes it safe anyway: I verified (by reading `plan_version`/`apply_version_plan` in `callisto-graph`, not by assuming) that `callisto version`'s write set is scoped to `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` manifests, `CHANGELOG.md` files, and `.changeset/*.md` — nothing else. So `HEAD`'s `.github/workflows` tree is byte-identical before and after that step runs. The pre-check isn't approximating the post-rebase state — it's already reading the exact same tree the post-rebase commit will have at that path, because that path is untouched by the step in between.

That said, right now that correctness rests on an *implicit* invariant (what `callisto version` happens to write), not an *enforced* one — so if that command's scope ever silently grew, this check would go stale without anyone noticing. That's worth closing regardless of whether it's a live bug today. Let me add a runtime assertion that fails loudly if that invariant is ever violated, so the guarantee becomes structural instead of "true because nothing currently contradicts it."

to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.

---

## Repository durable-release workflow

Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
removed from `main` until that PR is merged.

The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. GitHub's built-in workflow token can refuse
to force-update that long-lived branch after `main` has changed a workflow. In that uncommon
case Callisto automatically creates a SHA-suffixed replacement branch and release PR from the
same current `main` and changesets, then closes the superseded PR with a link. No publishing
credential or elevated GitHub token is required; subsequent ordinary updates continue on the
replacement PR. Repositories that require the same PR number through that GitHub-specific edge
case may optionally provide an App or fine-grained token with workflow-write authority to both
checkout and `callisto-action`'s `github_token` input.

After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.

Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure

This confirms it directly, and also answers your knope/changesets comparison well:

Now on the knope/changesets comparison — good instinct, and the answer is: **no, and deliberately not**, for a reason specific to this problem. Changesets (the JS tool) and knope both do exactly what you're describing: checkout the base branch, apply the accumulated version-bump patch on top (effectively a rebase/replay), and push. That works fine for them because their generated diff (version bumps + changelog text) is small and their branch update model tolerates a plain force-push.

Callisto's docs explicitly call out *why it doesn't do that* — from `docs/06-publishing.md`:

> This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward.

The distinction: a rebase *replays an old patch* onto a new base. Recomputation *reruns the generator* (`callisto version`) fresh against current `main` and currently-pending changesets. Those give the same result only when nothing changed between generations. If a changeset was added, removed, or edited since the branch was last built, a replayed old patch would be wrong (stale version bump, missing/extra changelog entries) — recomputing from scratch is always correct. That's a deliberate design choice, not an oversight, and it's *separate* from the GitHub-workflow-token issue we spent the last several turns on (that one — the supersede behavior — is a secondary, narrower edge case this same doc paragraph also covers, with the exact "GitHub's built-in workflow token can refuse..." explanation, and even notes the workaround: give it a workflow-scoped token if you want the same PR number preserved through that edge case).

So: checkout+rebase+run is the changesets/knope model; checkout+regenerate is Callisto's, chosen specifically to avoid stale generated content, and the workflow-token supersede logic rides along on top of that for the reasons already traced through.

Good catch, and I tried to pull the actual prior-session resolution to cross-check myself, but that path (`.entire/metadata/...`) is blocked by policy here — raw session transcripts aren't something I'll read even from git history. So this is me working it through fresh, not fishing for a script I found.

Here's the resolution, and it hinges on separating two different things I was blurring together:

**The final release PR's content is always workflow-free — you're right about that, unconditionally.** Once branch `callisto/version-packages--<sha>` exists, `git diff main...that-branch -- .github/workflows` is empty, always, because the branch is built as `current main tip + version bump`, and the version bump never touches that path. Confirmed by PR #28's actual file list earlier (zero workflow files) and by #48's, which will be the same.

**The rejection isn't about the PR's eventual content — it's about the mechanics of one specific push.** GitHub's workflow-file protection, as far as I can reason from how a pre-receive hook would actually have to work, evaluates a **two-point diff on the specific ref being updated**: old-tip-of-that-ref vs. new-tip-being-pushed, restricted to `.github/workflows/*`. It's not "does the final content match the current default branch" — it's "is this ref's own tree at that path changing, as part of this push." 

So: `callisto/version-packages` (PR #28's branch) was last pushed back on Aug 28, with whatever workflow files existed then. `main`'s workflow files changed since (via #38–46, merged normally, by a properly-privileged actor — merges go through the GitHub API, not a restricted-token `git push`, so that's a completely separate, unrestricted code path). Now, force-pushing an update to `callisto/version-packages` — even content built from current `main` — means *that specific ref's* stored tree transitions from old-workflow-content to new-workflow-content. GitHub blocks that transition for the unprivileged `GITHUB_TOKEN`, full stop, even though the new content already exists elsewhere in the repo (on `main`) — the check is ref-local, not "does this content already exist somewhere in the repository."

Once you sidestep that by creating a brand-new branch instead (which never had *any* prior stored state to diff against — its "old tip" doesn't exist), the push introduces the branch fresh, with content that matches `main` from the start, and there's nothing to reject.

So to directly answer: it's not that a workflow change "makes it into" the release PR — it never does, confirmed twice now. It's that *updating the old ref specifically* requires transitioning that ref's stored workflow content, which the restricted token can't do, regardless of where else in the repo that same content already lives.
That means we can allow force push from our action to the branch by specific name right? That is a config that each user would need to make but should be ok?

Not quite — it's not a branch-level setting, so "force push allowed for this branch name" doesn't exist as a knob that fixes it. The restriction lives on the **credential's own permission scope**, evaluated against the `.github/workflows/*` path regardless of which branch, regardless of branch protection rules, regardless of force-vs-non-force. Branch protection controls things like "who can push here" and "is force-push allowed on this branch" — orthogonal knobs. This restriction is GitHub refusing to let a token that lacks the `workflows` permission touch that path at all, full stop, anywhere in the repo.

The `GITHUB_TOKEN` GitHub mints automatically for an Actions run structurally cannot be granted `workflows` permission — it's not one of the scopes exposed in the workflow's `permissions:` block (unlike `contents`, `pull-requests`, etc.). So there's no config on the token itself either.

What actually works is swapping in a *different* credential for that one push — and Callisto's own docs already say this is the intended override, in `docs/06-publishing.md`:

> Repositories that require the same PR number through that GitHub-specific edge case may optionally provide an App or fine-grained token with workflow-write authority to both checkout and `callisto-action`'s `github_token` input.

Concretely, that means each repo that wants plain updates instead of the supersede dance would need to:
1. Create a fine-grained PAT (or a GitHub App installation) with `contents: write` + `workflows: write`, stored as a repo/org secret.
2. Pass it as `checkout`'s `token:` input *and* `callisto-action`'s `github_token:` input in their own `callisto-release.yml`.

That's real per-repo setup, and it's a materially bigger trust footprint than the default — that credential can now rewrite CI itself, which is exactly the elevated-privilege scenario the whole default-token design was trying to avoid. So it's correctly framed as opt-in, not something to make the default. Worth noting: this doesn't need any code change on Callisto's side — the `github_token` input and the supersede fallback already coexist as designed; a user just wires in a stronger token if they want to trade that safety margin for PR-number continuity.
I don't want to add a PAT, that is more complicated and this might explain why changeset and knope do rebases. I feel like this won't be a problem if we rebase, right?

No — and I can show this cleanly without more hedging: a rebase and Callisto's "recompute" approach would produce the *exact same final tree* here (no conflicts exist between the version-bump diff and whatever changed in workflows), so they're indistinguishable to GitHub at push time. GitHub's server only sees "here are new git objects, please move this ref from SHA A to SHA B" — it can't tell whether those objects came from `git rebase`, `git cherry-pick`, or a freshly authored commit. If the resulting tree is identical, the push either succeeds or fails identically regardless of which local git command built it.

I found relevant information about the issue you're searching for. Here are the key findings:

## Main Issue

The error "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow" occurs because, after creating a personal access token (PAT) with workflow permissions, it's necessary to copy this key and add it as a secret at the repository's secrets.

## Solution

After creating a PAT with workflow permissions, you need to copy the token and add it as a secret at the repository's secrets (Repo > Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions), and only after that can you use this repository secret within the workflow's `with` section.

## Changesets Action Specific

For the changesets/action specifically, in your repository settings, in Actions > General, ensure the "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" option is enabled.

## Related Issue

There's also a note that GitHub Apps need the `workflows` permission to create or update workflow files, which is another potential cause of this error.

The search results show this is a common issue when workflows attempt to create or update workflow files without proper permissions configured.

That settles it — `changesets/action` (the actual GitHub Action changesets ships) hits this exact same wall. It's a well-documented class of issue, and the fix the community lands on for it is identical to what Callisto's docs already recommend: a PAT with `workflow` permission wired into the action.

So the theory "changesets/knope must rebase their way around this" doesn't hold — they don't have a trick that avoids it, because there isn't one to have. It's not a Callisto-specific gap; it's a property of GitHub's `GITHUB_TOKEN` that applies to any tool doing this kind of "regenerate and force-push a long-lived branch" release-PR pattern, changesets included. When their release-PR branch goes stale against a base branch whose workflow files moved, their users hit the identical rejection and reach for the identical PAT-based workaround.

Given you don't want to add a PAT, Callisto's supersede behavior (close old PR, open a fresh one, link between them) is genuinely the least-bad default here — not a workaround Callisto uniquely needs because of some implementation gap, but the actual state of the art for this problem without handing the workflow a more powerful credential. I'd leave it as-is.

You were right, and I was wrong — not lying, but I gave you a confident conclusion off a shallow web search instead of actually checking, which had the same effect as being wrong on purpose. I went and read changesets/action's actual source instead of guessing this time. Here's what's really going on:

**Changesets/action does not use `git push` by default.** Its `pushChanges` function (`src/github.ts`) has two paths:
- Default: calls `commitChangesSinceBase()` from `@changesets/ghcommit`, which commits via GitHub's **`createCommitOnBranch` GraphQL mutation** — the same API GitHub's own web UI uses when you edit a file in the browser.
- Opt-in only (`push-with-git-cli: true`): falls back to literal `git push origin HEAD:branch --force`.

Callisto's script always does the second thing — a raw `git push --force-with-lease`. That's the actual difference, and it's a real, structural one, not a rebase-vs-recompute distinction. `changesets/ghcommit`'s own README states the API-based approach's specific reason for existing: to get GitHub-signed, verified commits attributed to the token's actor without needing local git credentials or GPG key management for bot commits — i.e., it's a purpose-built alternative to `git push` for exactly this kind of CI-bot scenario.

I can't swear with total certainty (short of an actual empirical test against a real diverged branch) that `createCommitOnBranch` is exempt from the `.github/workflows`-write restriction the way raw `git push` isn't — but the circumstantial case is strong: it's changesets' universal default across a huge number of repos, and "changesets breaks every time your workflow files change" isn't a known widespread complaint the way custom-git-push workflow-file issues are.

So the real fix isn't a PAT, and it isn't rebase — it's switching Callisto's executor script from `git push` to the same `createCommitOnBranch` GraphQL approach (or the equivalent REST Git Data API calls) for updating the release branch. That's a legitimate architecture change worth doing, not a quick tweak — it touches how the script authenticates and commits, and probably deserves its own spec given how this codebase handles changes. Want me to scope that out properly instead of patching around it further?

Let's think through this problem deeply, ensure that we understand it. Take into account our overall architecture, semantic models and scope out what the change would look like. What spec do we have to update? Make a plan and present it.

Before I write the plan I want to pin down two things precisely: how `ghcommit` actually sequences the ref move + commit (it determines the executor design), and what our semantic model/specs say about this boundary. Let me gather that.

# Release PR: commit via GitHub API instead of `git push` (drop supersede)

## Context

**Problem.** `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` maintains the long-lived managed release branch by regenerating it from current `main` (`callisto version`) and `git push --force-with-lease`-ing it with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That token cannot push content that changes `.github/workflows/*` on a ref. Whenever `main`'s workflow files change after the release branch was cut, the regenerated branch differs from the stale one at that path and the push is rejected. Today's mitigation (`workflowDeltaFromBase` in the snapshot, `ReleasePrActionV1::Supersede`) closes the old PR and opens a new SHA-suffixed one (what happened to #28 -> #48). The maintainer does not want PR churn and will not add a PAT.

**Discovery.** `changesets/action` does not `git push` by default. Its `@changesets/ghcommit` `commitChangesSinceBase(force: true)` path (ghcommit `src/core.ts`, "FORCE UPDATE"):
1. create/force-update a temp branch `changesets-ghcommit-temp/<branch>` at the base sha (REST `git.createRef`/`git.updateRef`)
2. GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` on the temp branch with `expectedHeadOid = base sha` and `fileChanges { additions[{path, contents(base64)}], deletions[{path}] }` containing only generated files
3. REST `git.updateRef(force: true)` moves the real branch to the new commit
4. delete the temp branch (also on failure)

Their code comment: "We cannot reset the branch and then commit because if the branch has an existing PR, GitHub will auto-close as it sees there's no changes with the base." The token never *creates* workflow-file content (new commit's parent is `main`, whose workflows are already current; the ref move points at an existing commit) so the restriction is never triggered. Bonus: API commits are GitHub-signed (Verified) and attributed to `github-actions[bot]`.

**Not yet proven.** We have not confirmed in a real Actions run that (a) raw `git push` is actually rejected in our scenario, and (b) the API flow succeeds with the default token when workflows diverged. Phase 0 is a falsifiable spike with GO/NO-GO before any code changes.

**Outcome.** One stable `callisto/version-packages` PR updated in place forever, no PAT, no `Supersede`, simpler snapshot (no per-PR `git fetch`/diff), Verified bot commits.

## Existing code to reuse

- `crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs` -- `ReleasePrConfigV1`, `ReleasePrSnapshotV1`, `ReleasePrPullRequestV1`, `ReleasePrActionV1`, `ReleasePrDecisionV1::{derive, verify_snapshot}`, `managed_branch_shape`, `Wire` + `SCHEMA_VERSION` deserialize pattern.
- `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release_pr.rs` -- `decide`/`verify` handlers; `read_json_arg`, `write_json`, `load_workspace`, `CliCommandRunner`.
- `crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs` -- `ReleasePrArgs { Decide, Verify }`.
- `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh` -- `release_pr_snapshot()`, decision `case`, two `release-pr verify` re-observations.
- Tests: `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh` (stubbed control-flow), `test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh` (real binary through the script's jq).
- Specs: `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-PR-DECISION-014.json` (AC-002..AC-005), `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json` (version-PR flow AC, revision_note). Plan: `.claude/plans/PLAN-RELEASE-PR-DECISION-014.json`.
- Docs: `docs/06-publishing.md` ("Repository durable-release workflow" paragraph).

## Findings that reshape the problem

1. **Spike question (a) is already answered empirically.** Release run `33679599559` on this repo (2026-09-02T20:43, head `3da710fe`) failed with the exact rejection:
   `! [remote rejected] callisto/version-packages -> callisto/version-packages (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission)`.
   Raw `git push` of a regenerated branch is rejected. Only question (b), the API path, needs a spike.
2. **Live state confirms other constraints.** PR #48's head commit `e823dd73` is `verification.verified: false, reason: unsigned` (author `github-actions[bot]`). No rulesets exist on `main` or `callisto/version-packages` (`/rules/branches/...` returns `[]`). The repo allows merge, squash, and rebase merges. `callisto version` already stages its own writes via `git add`/`git rm --cached` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` ~440-470), so the Git index after `version` is the authoritative change set. Current release payload is small: all CHANGELOGs total ~47 KB; a full plan is ~150-200 KB base64.

## Recommendations per design question

### Q1: Where to build the createCommitOnBranch payload -> (B) Rust `callisto release-pr commit-plan`

Rationale:
- Spec 014 architecture.execution says the shell "does not independently choose" anything and AC-004 forbids caller-controlled jq filtering. Deciding which paths are additions vs deletions, what to do with mode changes, renames, `.github/workflows/` paths, non-UTF-8 paths, and size limits is file-semantics policy; it belongs in typed Rust with unit tests, not in `git status --porcelain` parsing in bash (which cannot handle paths with spaces/newlines/quotes robustly).
- createCommitOnBranch cannot express modes (100755, 120000 symlink, 160000 submodule) or renames/type changes. A Rust builder can fail closed with typed miette errors; bash would silently strip the executable bit.
- Payload bytes must be read from the worktree as raw bytes (`std::fs::read`), not via `CommandRunner` whose `CommandOutput.stdout` is `String` (lossy UTF-8; see `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs:39`). CRLF and binary files round-trip only if bytes are never decoded.
- Testability: pure `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes(...)` in `callisto-model` is unit-testable; the Git observation goes through `CommandRunner` and is testable with the recording runner pattern already used in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` tests.
- Provider neutrality: the plan is `{baseCommit, message, additions[{path, contentsBase64}], deletions[{path}]}`; the shell does one mechanical jq mapping to GraphQL `FileChanges`. That mapping is covered by the real-binary contract test (the exact class of bug that shipped before).

Layering: plan types + builder + base64 in `callisto-model` (add `base64 = "0.22"`, MIT/Apache-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock`); raw-diff parsing and worktree reads in `callisto-vcs` (`ShellGit`, permissive); CLI wiring in `callisto-cli`.

Add a byte-fidelity invariant that makes the encoding question moot: the executor computes `local_tree=$(git write-tree)` after staging and, after createCommitOnBranch, compares it with `gh api repos/.../git/commits/<new_sha> --jq .tree.sha`. Equal tree OIDs prove the API commit is byte-identical to what Git would have committed (modes, CRLF, binary, everything). Fail before moving the real branch if they differ.

### Q2: Executor sequence and race safety

Snapshot gains `headCommit` per PR (`gh pr list --json headRefOid`) and drops `workflowDeltaFromBase` (which also removes the per-PR `git fetch` + `git diff` loop). Callisto names the staging branch in the decision so the shell never invents a branch name.

Sequence (`create-or-update-release-pr.sh`):
1. `base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`; `snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)`.
2. `decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide ...)`; branch on `kind` (noop|create|update). Read `.action.branch`, `.action.stagingBranch`, `.action.expectedHeadCommit` (update only), `.action.pullRequestNumber`.
3. Compose body (unchanged).
4. `$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND`; `git add -A` (parity for custom version commands).
5. `callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-pr-commit-plan.json"` (replaces the `git status --porcelain` emptiness check: empty plan is a typed error).
6. `local_tree=$(git write-tree)`.
7. Register `trap` that deletes the staging ref (`gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/<staging>`, tolerate 422/404 with a `::warning::`).
8. Verify #1 (`release-pr verify`) with a fresh snapshot.
9. Staging ref at base: `gh api -X PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<staging> -f sha=$base_commit -F force=true`, falling back to `POST .../git/refs` when the PATCH returns 422 (ref missing).
10. `new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq .data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid)` where `body.json` is built by jq from the plan: `expectedHeadOid: .baseCommit`, `branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner, branchName: <staging>}`, `fileChanges: {additions: [.additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}], deletions: .deletions}`.
11. `remote_tree=$(gh api .../git/commits/$new_sha --jq .tree.sha)`; require `== $local_tree`.
12. Verify #2 with a fresh snapshot (the `headCommit` field makes this the compare-and-swap surrogate for the PR head).
13. Move the real branch: update -> `PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<branch> -f sha=$new_sha -F force=true`; create -> `POST .../git/refs`, falling back to PATCH-force if it already exists (an orphan from a failed prior run; no PR exists on it by construction). Then GET the ref and require `.object.sha == $new_sha` (detects a lost race after the fact; fail loudly).
14. Verify #3, label, `gh pr create` / `gh pr edit` (unchanged).
15. Trap deletes staging branch (also runs on failure). Run to completion; report but do not fail on cleanup failure since the next run force-updates the deterministic staging name anyway.

Staging branch name: deterministic, derived by Callisto: `format!("{release_branch}--staging")`. Deterministic beats random because leftover refs from crashed runs are reclaimed rather than accumulating, and the workflow's `concurrency` group (`durable-release-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) already serializes runs. `managed_branch_shape` today returns `MalformedManagedBranch` for `--staging` (suffix is not 40-hex), so a PR opened from it already fails closed; add an explicit `ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` so the diagnostic is clear. Also update the `release-candidate` job regex? Not needed: `--staging` does not match `--[0-9a-f]{40}`.

Race safety honesty: REST `updateRef` has no CAS. The window between verify #2 and step 13 is milliseconds; the workflow concurrency group excludes the only automated racer; the post-move GET catches a human push in that window. That is acceptable and should be stated in the spec as the residual.

- Remove, do not reserve. A "fall back to supersede on 403" would make the shell branch on an HTTP status to choose an operation, which is exactly the policy-in-shell the spec forbids, and it keeps the branch-fetch/diff machinery alive for a path the spike either proves unnecessary or proves the whole plan dead. If NO-GO, nothing ships; the current code stays.
- Schema honesty: `ReleasePrSnapshotV1` is `deny_unknown_fields` and consumed by binaries that can be installed independently of the action script (`setup-callisto` with `source: auto` downloads the latest release), so field changes must be a real version bump. Introduce `ReleasePrPullRequestV2 { number, head_repository, head_branch, head_commit: CommitSha }`, `ReleasePrSnapshotV2` (schema 2), `ReleasePrActionV2 { Noop{reason}, Create{branch, staging_branch}, Update{pull_request_number, branch, expected_head_commit, staging_branch} }`, `ReleasePrDecisionV2` (schema 2), and delete the V1 types. Old action script + new binary fails closed with "unsupported release PR snapshot schema version"; new script + old binary fails the same way. Keep `#[non_exhaustive]`, `deny_unknown_fields`, the `Wire` schema-version check, and the `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` fix.

# Release PR: commit via GitHub API instead of `git push` (retire supersede)

## Context

**Problem.** `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` maintains the long-lived managed release branch by regenerating it from current `main` (`callisto version`) and `git push --force-with-lease`-ing it with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That token cannot push content that changes `.github/workflows/*` on a ref. Whenever `main`'s workflow files change after the release branch was cut, the regenerated branch differs from the stale one at that path and the push is rejected. Proven on this repo: run `33679599559` (2026-09-02) failed with `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission`. Today's mitigation (`workflowDeltaFromBase` in the snapshot -> `ReleasePrActionV1::Supersede`) closes the old PR and opens a SHA-suffixed one (#28 -> #48). Maintainer wants one stable PR and no PAT.

**Discovery.** `changesets/action` never `git push`es by default. `@changesets/ghcommit` `commitChangesSinceBase(force: true)` (its `src/core.ts` "FORCE UPDATE" path):
1. create/force-update a temp branch at the base sha (REST `git.createRef` / `git.updateRef`)
2. GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` on the temp branch, `expectedHeadOid = base sha`, `fileChanges { additions[{path, contents(base64)}], deletions[{path}] }` = only the generated files
3. REST `git.updateRef(force: true)` moves the real branch to the new commit
4. delete the temp branch (also on failure)

Their comment: "We cannot reset the branch and then commit because if the branch has an existing PR, GitHub will auto-close as it sees there's no changes with the base." The token never *creates* workflow content (new commit's parent is `main`, whose workflows are current; the ref move points at an existing commit), so the restriction is never hit. Bonus: API commits are GitHub-signed (Verified) and attributed to `github-actions[bot]` (PR #48's head `e823dd73` is currently `verified: false, reason: unsigned`).

**Unproven and load-bearing.** Nothing confirms the API path succeeds with the default token when workflows diverged. It cannot be tested from a dev machine (personal `gh` tokens carry `workflow` scope). Phase 0 is a falsifiable spike with a GO/NO-GO gate; no code ships on NO-GO.

**Outcome.** One stable `callisto/version-packages` PR updated in place indefinitely, no PAT, `Supersede` + per-PR `git fetch`/diff removed, Verified bot commits, version-PR job holds no git push credentials.

## Decisions already made (maintainer)
- Spike runs in a throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike` (created, used, deleted).
- `version-pr` checkout flips to `persist-credentials: false` in the same change (drop the zizmor ignore).
- One PR for model + CLI + action, opened only after spike GO.
- `setup_git_user` input stays accepted as a documented no-op for now (removing it is consumer-visible); revisit in a breaking release.
- Payload cap is a constant set from spike measurements (no escape-hatch flag).

## Phase 0: spike (GO/NO-GO gate)

Throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`, default branch `main` with `.github/workflows/spike.yml` (workflow_dispatch, input `case`, `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write`, checkout `persist-credentials: false`) and `.github/workflows/dummy.yml`. Setup: branch `managed` cut from `main` with a `VERSION` file + PR opened; then change `dummy.yml` on `main` so workflows diverge. Each case writes its result to the job summary.

| Case | What | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| A | regenerate `managed` from `main` locally, `git push --force-with-lease` with GITHUB_TOKEN | rejected (control; matches run 33679599559) |
| B | `git push --force origin <main sha>:refs/heads/managed` (git-only ref move) | rejected (confirms git-only alternative is dead) |
| C | temp ref at `main` sha -> `createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=main)` with `VERSION` edit, one deletion, a CRLF file, a small PNG -> `updateRef(force)` `managed` -> delete temp | success; PR still open; PR files == intended set; `verification.verified == true`; `commit.tree.sha == local git write-tree` |
| D | case C with stale `expectedHeadOid` | `createCommitOnBranch` errors (CAS confirmed) |
| E | additions of 1, 8, 32 MiB text | record first failure and error text -> `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` |
| F | case C twice with no change | PR stays open (no auto-close on reruns) |

GO: C succeeds with diverged workflows, PR stays open and updated in place, tree OIDs equal, D errors, E limit >= 4 MiB, verified == true.
NO-GO: C rejected with the workflows-permission error, or PR auto-closes -> stop, keep supersede, record evidence in spec 013's `revision_note`.
Record all outcomes in `PLAN-RELEASE-PR-API-COMMIT-015.json` `evidence`.

## Design

### Payload built in Rust, not bash (`callisto release-pr commit-plan`)
Spec 014 forbids policy in the shell; deciding additions vs deletions, refusing modes/renames/symlinks (which `createCommitOnBranch` cannot express), refusing `.github/workflows/` paths, byte-faithful contents (CRLF/binary must be read with `std::fs::read`, not the lossy `String` stdout of `CommandRunner`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs`), and size limits are file-semantics policy that needs unit tests. The shell does one mechanical jq mapping to GraphQL `FileChanges`, covered by the real-binary contract test.

`callisto version` already stages its writes (`git add` / `git rm --cached` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` ~440-470), so the index vs base commit is the authoritative change set.

Byte-fidelity invariant in the executor: `local_tree=$(git write-tree)` after staging must equal `gh api .../git/commits/<new_sha> --jq .tree.sha` before the real branch moves. Equal tree OIDs prove the API commit is byte-identical to what git would have committed.

### Types (`crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs`)
Replace V1 with V2 (snapshot is `deny_unknown_fields` and binaries can be installed independently of the script via `setup-callisto source: auto`, so this must be a real version bump; keep `Wire` + `SCHEMA_VERSION` check, `#[non_exhaustive]`, and `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"`):
- `ReleasePrPullRequestV2 { number, head_repository, head_branch, head_commit: CommitSha }` (drop `workflow_delta_from_base`)
- `ReleasePrSnapshotV2` (schema 2), `ReleasePrDecisionV2` (schema 2)
- `ReleasePrActionV2 { Noop{reason}, Create{branch, staging_branch}, Update{pull_request_number, branch, expected_head_commit, staging_branch} }` -- no `Supersede`, no runtime fallback (a shell branching on a 403 to pick an operation is exactly the policy-in-shell the spec forbids).
- `staging_branch = format!("{release_branch}--staging")`, deterministic so crashed-run leftovers are reclaimed; `managed_branch_shape` already rejects it (suffix not 40-hex) -> add explicit `ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` (E154). Keep accepting `canonical--<40hex>` so PR #48 stays managed and is updated in place.
- `verify_snapshot` now also catches a moved PR head (`head_commit`) -- the compare-and-swap surrogate before the non-CAS `updateRef`.
- New `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1 { schema_version, base_commit, message, additions: Vec<{path, contents_base64}>, deletions: Vec<{path}>, total_content_bytes }` built by `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes(base, message, Vec<StagedChangeV1>)`; `StagedChangeV1 { path, kind: Added|Modified|Deleted|Renamed|Copied|TypeChanged|Unmerged, new_mode: Option<u32>, contents: Option<Vec<u8>> }`; `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` from spike E.
- Errors (E141-E148 taken; `DIAGNOSTIC_CODE_SOURCE_FILES` in `crates/callisto-model/src/lib.rs` already scans this file): `EmptyCommitPlan` E149, `UnsupportedFileMode` E150, `UnsupportedChangeKind` E151, `CommitPlanTooLarge` E152, `ForbiddenCommitPlanPath` E153 (`.github/workflows/`, `.git/`, `..`, absolute, non-UTF-8), `StagingBranchPullRequest` E154.
- Dependency: `base64 = "0.22"` (MIT/Apache-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock`) in workspace + `callisto-model`.

### VCS observation (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` or new `staged.rs`)
`ShellGit::staged_changes_since(&self, base: &CommitSha) -> Result<Vec<StagedChangeV1>, VcsError>`: `git diff --cached --raw -z --no-renames <base>`, parse mode/status/path, read A/M contents with `std::fs::read`. Recording-runner tests as in existing `shell.rs` tests.

# Release PR: commit via GitHub API instead of `git push` (retire supersede)

## Context

**Problem.** `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` maintains the long-lived managed release branch by regenerating it from current `main` (`callisto version`) and `git push --force-with-lease`-ing it with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That token cannot push content that changes `.github/workflows/*` on a ref. Whenever `main`'s workflow files change after the release branch was cut, the regenerated branch differs from the stale one at that path and the push is rejected. Proven on this repo: run `33679599559` (2026-09-02) failed with `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission`. Today's mitigation (`workflowDeltaFromBase` in the snapshot -> `ReleasePrActionV1::Supersede`) closes the old PR and opens a SHA-suffixed one (#28 -> #48). Maintainer wants one stable PR and no PAT.

**Discovery.** `changesets/action` never `git push`es by default. `@changesets/ghcommit` `commitChangesSinceBase(force: true)` (its `src/core.ts` "FORCE UPDATE" path):
1. create/force-update a temp branch at the base sha (REST `git.createRef` / `git.updateRef`)
2. GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` on the temp branch, `expectedHeadOid = base sha`, `fileChanges { additions[{path, contents(base64)}], deletions[{path}] }` = only the generated files
3. REST `git.updateRef(force: true)` moves the real branch to the new commit
4. delete the temp branch (also on failure)

Their comment: "We cannot reset the branch and then commit because if the branch has an existing PR, GitHub will auto-close as it sees there's no changes with the base." The token never *creates* workflow content (new commit's parent is `main`, whose workflows are current; the ref move points at an existing commit), so the restriction is never hit. Bonus: API commits are GitHub-signed (Verified) and attributed to `github-actions[bot]` (PR #48's head `e823dd73` is currently `verified: false, reason: unsigned`).

**Unproven and load-bearing.** Nothing confirms the API path succeeds with the default token when workflows diverged. It cannot be tested from a dev machine (personal `gh` tokens carry `workflow` scope). Phase 0 is a falsifiable spike with a GO/NO-GO gate; no code ships on NO-GO.

**Outcome.** One stable `callisto/version-packages` PR updated in place indefinitely, no PAT, `Supersede` + per-PR `git fetch`/diff removed, Verified bot commits, version-PR job holds no git push credentials.

## Decisions already made (maintainer)
- Spike runs in a throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike` (created, used, deleted).
- `version-pr` checkout flips to `persist-credentials: false` in the same change (drop the zizmor ignore).
- One PR for model + CLI + action, opened only after spike GO.
- `setup_git_user` input stays accepted as a documented no-op for now (removing it is consumer-visible); revisit in a breaking release.
- Payload cap is a constant set from spike measurements (no escape-hatch flag).

## Phase 0: spike (GO/NO-GO gate)

Throwaway repo `orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`, default branch `main` with `.github/workflows/spike.yml` (workflow_dispatch, input `case`, `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write`, checkout `persist-credentials: false`) and `.github/workflows/dummy.yml`. Setup: branch `managed` cut from `main` with a `VERSION` file + PR opened; then change `dummy.yml` on `main` so workflows diverge. Each case writes its result to the job summary.

| Case | What | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| A | regenerate `managed` from `main` locally, `git push --force-with-lease` with GITHUB_TOKEN | rejected (control; matches run 33679599559) |
| B | `git push --force origin <main sha>:refs/heads/managed` (git-only ref move) | rejected (confirms git-only alternative is dead) |
| C | temp ref at `main` sha -> `createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=main)` with `VERSION` edit, one deletion, a CRLF file, a small PNG -> `updateRef(force)` `managed` -> delete temp | success; PR still open; PR files == intended set; `verification.verified == true`; `commit.tree.sha == local git write-tree` |
| D | case C with stale `expectedHeadOid` | `createCommitOnBranch` errors (CAS confirmed) |
| E | additions of 1, 8, 32 MiB text | record first failure and error text -> `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` |
| F | case C twice with no change | PR stays open (no auto-close on reruns) |

GO: C succeeds with diverged workflows, PR stays open and updated in place, tree OIDs equal, D errors, E limit >= 4 MiB, verified == true.
NO-GO: C rejected with the workflows-permission error, or PR auto-closes -> stop, keep supersede, record evidence in spec 013's `revision_note`.
Record all outcomes in `PLAN-RELEASE-PR-API-COMMIT-015.json` `evidence`.

## Design

### Payload built in Rust, not bash (`callisto release-pr commit-plan`)
Spec 014 forbids policy in the shell; deciding additions vs deletions, refusing modes/renames/symlinks (which `createCommitOnBranch` cannot express), refusing `.github/workflows/` paths, byte-faithful contents (CRLF/binary must be read with `std::fs::read`, not the lossy `String` stdout of `CommandRunner`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs`), and size limits are file-semantics policy that needs unit tests. The shell does one mechanical jq mapping to GraphQL `FileChanges`, covered by the real-binary contract test.

`callisto version` already stages its writes (`git add` / `git rm --cached` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` ~440-470), so the index vs base commit is the authoritative change set.

Byte-fidelity invariant in the executor: `local_tree=$(git write-tree)` after staging must equal `gh api .../git/commits/<new_sha> --jq .tree.sha` before the real branch moves. Equal tree OIDs prove the API commit is byte-identical to what git would have committed.

### Types (`crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs`)

- `ReleasePrActionV2 { Noop{reason}, Create{branch, staging_branch}, Update{pull_request_number, branch, expected_head_commit, staging_branch} }` -- no `Supersede`, no runtime fallback (a shell branching on a 403 to pick an operation is exactly the policy-in-shell the spec forbids).
- `staging_branch = format!("{release_branch}--staging")`, deterministic so crashed-run leftovers are reclaimed; `managed_branch_shape` already rejects it (suffix not 40-hex) -> add explicit `ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` (E154). - Dependency: `base64 = "0.22"` (MIT/Apache-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock`) in workspace + `callisto-model`.

### VCS observation (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` or new `staged.rs`)
`ShellGit::staged_changes_since(&self, base: &CommitSha) -> Result<Vec<StagedChangeV1>, VcsError>`: `git diff --cached --raw -z --no-renames <base>`, parse mode/status/path, read A/M contents with `std::fs::read`. Expose through `GitAccess` the same way `observe_git_commit_trust` delegates to the shell backend (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs:108`); nothing in `GitDataSource`/gix today lists changed paths or reads blobs, so this is new surface, shell-only. Recording-runner tests as in existing `shell.rs` tests (fake at ~:474).

### CLI (`crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs`, `commands/release_pr.rs`)
`ReleasePrArgs::CommitPlan(ReleasePrCommitPlanArgs { base_commit, message, out: Option<PathBuf> })`; `--out` writes via `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`, else JSON to stdout via `write_json`; update `render_decision` for V2 (drop the `Supersede` arm, keep the `_ =>` arm for `#[non_exhaustive]`); `verify` currently emits a hard-coded `{"schemaVersion": 1, "ok": true}` (`commands/release_pr.rs:31`) -- tie it to `ReleasePrDecisionV2::SCHEMA_VERSION`; update the `Decide` doc comment at `cli.rs:268` ("create, update, supersede, or no-op" -> "create, update, or no-op"; rendered in `release-pr --help`, not snapshotted). `help.trycmd` snapshots only top-level `--help`; refresh only if the `release-pr` one-liner changes.
